nodes.name: A context window is not a memory.
nodes.text: ## A context window is not a memory.

nodes.name: A model’s context window is everything it can consider at…
nodes.text: A model’s context window is everything it can consider at once. It is large, and getting larger, but it is also temporary. When the session ends, the window is gone. The next session starts from whatever it is given.

nodes.name: That makes context windows good at holding a task and poor…
nodes.text: That makes context windows good at holding a task and poor at holding a team’s knowledge. A window can hold the decision you made this morning. It cannot remember, next week, that the decision was made, who made it, or that it was later reversed. Putting more text into each prompt does not fix this; it only moves the question of what is current into a longer prompt.

nodes.name: Memory, in the sense that matters for teams, is the…
nodes.text: Memory, in the sense that matters for teams, is the durable layer underneath: the place a session starts from, and the place a useful result goes back to.

nodes.name: Durable context is not a pile of notes. It needs an owner,…
nodes.text: Durable context is not a pile of notes. It needs an owner, a current version and a history. When an agent reads a file, it should know which revision it read. When it writes, it should state which revision it is replacing, so that a write based on stale information fails instead of overwriting newer work.

nodes.name: NullDull Memory works this way. Revisions are immutable…
nodes.text: NullDull Memory works this way. Revisions are immutable and attributed to the member an agent acts for. An excerpt from a search result is never treated as a complete read; to edit a file, an agent reads the whole current version first.

nodes.name: Agents produce plausible text quickly. That is useful, and…
nodes.text: Agents produce plausible text quickly. That is useful, and it is also why shared guidance needs review. A proposed change to a team’s deployment instructions should be seen by someone accountable for them before it becomes the instruction every other agent follows.

nodes.name: Memory keeps proposals separate from the current file.…
nodes.text: Memory keeps proposals separate from the current file. Junior access and propose-mode agents submit changes; an authorized Senior approves the exact candidate. When changes from different people need reconciling, the system surfaces contradictory decisions instead of choosing one. And an agent cannot approve the proposals of the person it represents—a second connection for the same person is not an independent reviewer.

nodes.name: The more useful shared context becomes, the more it…
nodes.text: The more useful shared context becomes, the more it matters who can retrieve it. Being in the same workspace should not mean every agent can read every file. Search and discovery in Memory filter by each member’s current access before results are returned, and a connection’s capabilities are intersected with the member’s own rights.

nodes.name: Generated content needs the same care. Before Null saves…
nodes.text: Generated content needs the same care. Before Null saves content derived from a conversation, it checks that everyone who can read the destination can also read every source used to produce it. Without that check, an agent could move a private detail into a shared file simply by summarizing it.

nodes.name: Know where an answer came from.
nodes.text: ## Know where an answer came from.

nodes.name: Retrieval is most useful when it is attributable. A search…
nodes.text: Retrieval is most useful when it is attributable. A search result in Memory comes with its current location and folder path, so a person or agent can see whether guidance came from the workspace root, a product or a specific project. Opening a result rereads the file and its current path rather than trusting an older excerpt.

nodes.name: This is the direction we are building toward more broadly:…
nodes.text: This is the direction we are building toward more broadly: context gathered for a project task from authorized workspace, product and project guidance, each item returned with its source and revision. A model can then cite what it used, and a person can check it. That is the difference between an agent that sounds confident and one whose work can be reviewed.
